articles.title: Spain’s housing crisis in focus after eviction of 87-year-old woman
articles.summary: The tenant of the flat in the Retiro area of central Madrid, Maricarmen, was unable to pay her rent set after it was increased by an investment firm.
articles.body:
An 87-year-old woman has been evicted from her home in Madrid where she has lived for seven decades, in a case which has put the spotlight on Spain's soaring rents and lack of available housing.

The tenant, known by her first name, Maricarmen, was removed from her flat in the Retiro area of central Madrid on Wednesday, with people taking part in a protest at her property clashing with police.

Maricarman was left unable to pay her rent after investment firm Urbagestión, which bought the property in 2018, increased it from €500 (£428; $572) to €2,650 (£2,280; $3,020) - although later offering to reduce this to €1,650 (a figure she was still unable to pay on her pension of €1,350).

articles.title: How to pack a winter emergency car kit, according to the NWS and DOT
articles.summary: Learn what to put in your winter car kit, plus shop pre-made kits and supplies like jump starters, flashlights, tire chains and more.
articles.body: Seventy percent of winter deaths related to snow and ice occur in cars, according to the Massachusetts Department of Transportation. Depending on where you live, wintertime can bring severe cold weather and snowstorms that can leave you stranded on the road. If that happens, a winter emergency car kit can be a lifesaver, according to the National Weather Service (NWS) and Vision Zero North Dakota. That’s why I collected guidance from government agencies like NWS and the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) about what to put in a winter emergency car kit, and recommend some top-rated kits and supplies below. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best winter emergency car kits of 2026 Our top picks have many of the supplies recommended by agencies like FEMA and the American Red Cross. You can supplement them with supplies of your own and find additional supplies in the kit supplies section. Best winter kit This is a great starter kit to supplement with your own supplies: it includes many of the items recommended by the agencies we mentioned above, including a first aid kit, ice scraper, and a few winter clothing items. It is light on car equipment, however, so you’ll want to add items like a jump starter or jumper cables, a tow rope and a tire inflator ASAP. Best general car kit This car emergency kit isn’t specific to winter conditions, so you’ll want to supplement it with cold-weather supplies. It includes a large first aid kit as well as many recommended car emergency supplies like reflective warning triangles and jumper cables. It also comes with a digital air compressor that can inflate standard tires in a few seconds, according to the brand. You can read a full list of the included supplies on Everlit Survival’s website. Top-rated winter emergency car kit supplies of 2026 Almost all pre-made kits are missing a few items, so it’s important to supplement them with tools and supplies depending on your needs. You may also prefer to build your own winter emergency car kit from scratch — you probably already have many of the items recommended by expert agencies. Below are highly rated winter emergency car kit supplies for you and your vehicle. Supplies for you First-aid kit Any first aid kit should include a variety of supplies for treating wounds and injuries. It’s important to add items like medications and emergency contacts, according to the American Red Cross. Water Water can be tricky to store in winter conditions — it may freeze if stored in the trunk or a flatbed, so we recommend storing it in the backseat or somewhere else in your vehicle’s main cabin, if possible. Flashlight A flashlight is a critical tool, especially if it’s dark out and you need to troubleshoot your vehicle. I include emergency flashlights and headlamps, which can keep your hands free. Cell phone, road maps Multiple agencies recommend keeping cell phone chargers and spare road maps as part of your emergency car kit. Batteries and portable chargers Most flashlights are powered by disposable AA or AAA batteries. A portable power bank is also good to have for keeping your phone charged. Non-perishable food The Massachusetts Department of Transportation recommends high-calorie, non-perishable foods like dried fruits and nuts and canned foods. If you need to sleep in your car, Vision Zero North Dakota recommends eating a snack of high-calorie food just before sleeping to stimulate your metabolism and heat production (a common practice in cold-weather camping). Blanket, mittens, boots, warm clothes Blankets, mittens, boots and warm clothes can all help keep you warm if you need to stay put during a roadside winter emergency. Supplies for your vehicle Jump starter/jumper cables Being able to jump-start your vehicle on your own or with the help of another vehicle is a critical part of any car kit. Tire chains Tire chains can give you more traction, especially on unpaved roads with snowy or icy conditions. Tire repair tools Having everything you need to repair a flat tire on the road can help prevent a winter roadside emergency before it happens. Gas Spare gas can mean the difference between being stranded and getting to your destination without incident. Shovel, ice scraper, snow brush Having tools to combat snow and ice is essential for winter emergencies — both can get your car stuck and block visibility in your windshield. Roadside lighting Repairing potential issues with your car is a lot safer the more visible you are to other vehicles. Tools like LED beacons and reflective triangles can help. Tow rope A tow rope can help get your car unstuck from snowy or icy conditions, with the assistance of another vehicle, of course. Sand, road salt or kitty litter (for traction) Sand, road salt and (surprisingly) kitty litter can give your tires added traction if you are trying to get your vehicle out of being stuck in place. How I picked top-rated emergency kits and supplies Using guidance from reputable agencies like the National Weather Service, FEMA, the American Red Cross and state and local departments of transportation, I selected emergency kits based on the following criteria: Supplies included: All of the above organizations suggest some variation of a winter car emergency kit that includes the following: First aid kitBasic tool kitFlashlightSustenance: Water and non-perishable foodWarmth: Blankets, warm clothes (boots, mittens, jackets, etc.)Communication: Portable charger and batteriesEmergency signal tools: flares, beacons, reflective triangles, whistleSnow tools: shovel, ice scraper, snow brushCar starting tools: jumper starter or jumper cables, extra gasTire tools: Tire chains, snow tires, tire repair kit and inflator, sand or cat litter (for traction)Towing tools: tow rope Top-rated: I only selected pre-made kits with at least a four-star rating from major retailers like Amazon. Why trust NBC Selected? Harry Rabinowitz is a former reporter at NBC Selected who covered technology and fitness, including stories on smartwatches, running shoes, wireless earbuds and more. He also covered home and health tools like air purifiers, air conditioners and blood pressure monitors. For this piece, he researched winter emergency car preparation guidelines from reputable government and local agencies to put together a list of recommended items. articles.title: Corretora morta em Itapira: Fabiola Araujo é assassinada em táxi | G1
articles.standfirst: Crime ocorreu em uma estrada rural na manhã desta quarta-feira (24). Segundo a Polícia Militar, suspeitos estavam de moto e fugiram.
articles.summary: Corretora morta em Itapira, Fabiola Fernandes Araujo foi baleada por homens em uma moto enquanto seguia de táxi para mostrar um imóvel rural.
articles.body:
Fabiola Fernandes Araujo, corretora de imóveis morta a tiros em Itapira (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram/Itapira News

Uma mulher foi assassinada a tiros dentro de um táxi na manhã desta quarta-feira (24), em uma estrada rural de Itapira (SP). A vítima foi identificada como Fabiola Fernandes Araujo , de 43 anos, corretora de imóveis em Águas de Lindóia (SP).

Fabiola seguia de táxi para apresentar uma propriedade a um comprador quando foi atacada por dois homens em uma moto. O motorista presenciou o crime, mas não foi ferido .

Segundo o corretor de imóveis Carlos de Jesus, Fabiola havia solicitado o táxi porque estava sem carro naquele dia.

" Nós tínhamos agendado com o comprador para apresentar uma propriedade. O vendedor é o nosso cliente, e ela ia trazer o comprador . Então, como ela não tinha carro, ela solicitou um táxi para levar ela até lá. E, no trajeto do caminho, depois que a gente passou por toda essa tragédia, ficamos sabendo que dois motoqueiros, inclusive, passaram por nós, pararam ela no meio do caminho, levaram a bolsa dela e deram os tiros. E ela acabou falecendo no carro", afirmou.

Carlos também descreveu Fabiola como uma profissional dedicada e disse que os dois já trabalhavam desde cedo no dia do crime .

"É uma pessoa dedicadíssima ao trabalho, sem preguiça para trabalhar. [...] tentando a todo momento querer vencer na vida, trabalhando honestamente. E, sem motivo aparente, acontecer tudo isso, a gente fica revoltado", disse.

O homicídio aconteceu em um trecho localizado logo à frente da entrada de uma chácara da região. Os criminosos fugiram após os disparos.

Ninguém havia sido preso até a última atualização desta reportagem. Também não há informações sobre o velório e o enterro de Fabiola.

articles.title: Cremesp abre sindicância contra ginecologista indiciado por estupro de paciente  | G1
articles.standfirst: Esther Neves passou por consultas com Osmar Trojan entre 2014 e 2022, em um consultório particular em São Paulo. Segundo a vítima, durante os atendimentos, ele fez exames sem luvas, tirou fotos íntimas dela e exibiu vídeos pornográficos. O médico nega as acusações.
articles.summary: Esther Neves passou por consultas com Osmar Trojan entre 2014 e 2022, em um consultório particular em São Paulo. Segundo a vítima, durante os atendimentos, ele fez exames sem luvas, tirou fotos íntimas dela e exibiu vídeos pornográficos. O médico nega as acusações.
articles.body:
O Conselho Regional de Medicina do Estado de São Paulo (Cremesp) instaurou uma sindicância para apurar a conduta do ginecologista Osmar Trojan, de 82 anos, indiciado pelo crime de estupro contra uma paciente . Segundo o órgão, o caso corre sob sigilo.

A sindicância é a fase preliminar para averiguação dos fatos denunciados, coleta de provas, manifestação escrita ou audiência com os envolvidos.

Caso sejam constatados indícios de infração ética, o Cremesp pode instaurar um processo ético-disciplinar. Nessa fase, denunciante e denunciado têm direito de apresentar provas e se manifestar, inclusive com acompanhamento de advogados.

Procurado, o advogado Alessandro Fischer Martins Silveira, que representa Osmar, negou as acusações e afirmou que "confia que, no curso da instrução processual, mediante o exercício pleno do contraditório e da ampla defesa e a produção das provas pertinentes, demonstrará sua inocência".

A defesa também ressaltou que o inquérito tramita sob sigilo e que, até o momento, não houve recebimento de denúncia pela Justiça. Segundo o advogado, o procedimento ainda está na fase de investigação e deve ser observada a presunção de inocência.

Esther Neves entrou pela primeira vez no consultório do ginecologista Osmar Trojan aos 16 anos. O médico era próximo de sua família, atendia sua mãe e era visto como uma espécie de figura paterna. Hoje, aos 27 anos, a jovem passou a entender de outra forma situações que, na época, acreditava fazerem parte das consultas.

A jovem foi atendida por Osmar entre 2014 e 2022 em um consultório particular no Brooklin, na Zona Sul de São Paulo.

Durante as consultas, ele fez exames sem luvas, tirou fotos íntimas dela e exibiu vídeos pornográficos. Em um dos episódios, ele chegou a sugar os seios dela sob a justificativa de verificar o que saía deles, segundo Esther.

"Ele não cobrava as consultas. Eu e a minha mãe sentíamos que a gente estava devendo algo para ele. Então quando ele falava que queria me fotografar, eu me sentia na obrigação de ir, porque ele falava que era uma coisa boa", contou Esther ao g1.

O ginecologista, de 82 anos, é investigado por estupro em inquérito policial instaurado no 1° Distrito Policial de Itapecerica da Serra, após pedido do Ministério Público.

Procurada, a Secretaria da Segurança Pública informou que "o homem foi formalmente indiciado pela prática do crime de estupro, previsto no artigo 213 do Código Penal". A pasta também disse que "as investigações prosseguem visando o devido esclarecimento dos fatos".

Ginecologista acusado de estupro — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

A relação de confiança entre Osmar e Esther, que hoje é advogada, foi construída ao longo de anos e se estendia para além do consultório.

Segundo o interrogatório do médico, ele conheceu a mãe da jovem em 1992, quando trabalhava como telefonista em um hospital onde também atendia. Os dois ficaram amigos e ele não cobrava pelas consultas por causa da amizade e da situação socioeconômica dela. Osmar também fez o parto de Esther.

Desde criança, Esther convivia com o ginecologista, que também frequentava a mesma igreja que a família, onde ministrava palestras.

“E eu acabei vendo ele também dessa forma, porque o meu avô morava em Tocantins. Então eu não tinha proximidade com pessoas no meu convívio. Aqui, em São Paulo, são só eu, minha mãe, meu pai e meu irmão.”

Aos 16 anos, em 2014, Esther passou pela primeira consulta com Osmar. Segundo ela, o médico sugeria que ela entrasse sozinha na sala para que ficasse mais à vontade.

Com o passar dos anos, os dois mantiveram contato frequente. Segundo Esther, o médico mandava mensagens, fotos de viagens e registros do que fazia no dia a dia. Ela também chegou a trabalhar no consultório dele por cerca de um mês para substituir a secretária durante as férias.

“Era muito próxima, ele mandava muitas mensagens. Era como se fosse meu pai. O contato que eu não tinha com meu pai, eu tinha com ele. Então, tudo que ele fazia, ele mandava mensagem. Ele mandava fotos minhas. Ele mandava fotos dele nas viagens. Tudo que ele fazia, ele mandava”, contou.

Esther afirma que chegou a comentar com a mãe que algumas situações com o médico pareciam estranhas. Segundo ela, a mãe dizia que cabia a ela interromper aquela relação, mas também ressaltava que Osmar era uma pessoa de confiança da família e nunca havia cobrado pelas consultas.

Na Unicamp, Osmar foi colega de turma de Roger Abdelmassih, ex-médico brasileiro e especialista em reprodução humana que foi condenado a mais de 270 anos de prisão por dezenas de estupros e crimes sexuais cometidos contra pacientes.

Dos 16 aos 24 anos, Esther relata ter sido submetida a uma série de situações de cunho sexual durante consultas com o ginecologista, sob a justificativa de que faziam parte de exames clínicos. Os atendimentos duravam cerca de duas horas, segundo ela, e incluíam toques que considerava desnecessários.

Em alguns atendimentos, segundo Esther, o médico exibia vídeos de um site pornográfico — mesmo quando ela ainda era adolescente. Segundo a jovem, ele mostrava uma mulher com tipo físico semelhante ao dela e usava o conteúdo para falar sobre o uso de um plugue anal.

“Ele assistia esse site e colocava uma pessoa com um tipo físico muito parecido com o meu, pesava mais ou menos uns 45 kg. E aí ele falava: ‘olha, essa menina é novinha igual a você. Você é linda, você é perfeita. Ela tem aqui um plugue anal. Se você quiser, eu posso comprar para você e eu te ensino a usar’”, contou.

Em outra consulta, Esther afirma que o médico a convenceu a fazer uma sessão de fotos no consultório, com os seios nus. Segundo ela, Osmar disse que estava escrevendo um artigo de conscientização sobre o câncer de mama e que costumava fotografar pacientes.

“Ele me mostrou uma relação de fotos de várias pacientes dele e falou: 'olha, você precisa fazer isso também, porque fazer um ensaio fotográfico é uma coisa muito cara. E eu sei que você não tem condição de pagar, então eu vou te fazer de graça [...] Eu fico com essas fotos e te dou em um pendrive."

Na época, segundo Esther, o médico também conversou com a mãe dela para pedir autorização. “Eu não lembro se eu era menor de idade, mas a minha mãe autorizou. E eu acabei autorizando também.”

Depois das fotos dos seios, Esther afirma que o médico passou a fotografar outras partes do corpo.

“Ele fotografou minhas mamas por causa do câncer de mama. Até aí, tudo bem. Só que aí, ele começou com uma história de que ele tinha pacientes muito complexadas com o tamanho dos grandes lábios da vagina delas [...] ele tirou muitas fotos da minha vagina também, do meu ânus.”

Em outra ocasião, Esther contou que o médico sugou seus seios durante uma consulta. Segundo ela, Osmar disse que o procedimento serviria para verificar o que saía das mamas. Ao longo dos atendimentos, o médico apresentava justificativas para os procedimentos e fazia com que ela acreditasse que aquelas situações faziam parte de uma consulta.

Esther diz que só conseguiu compreender que havia passado por situações abusivas depois de começar a tratar questões que já afetavam sua saúde mental. Segundo ela, a terapia foi o ponto de virada para perceber que situações que havia vivido nas consultas não eram parte normal de um atendimento médico.

Em 2024, a jovem chegou a ser internada após uma crise de ansiedade. Ela afirma que faz acompanhamento com um psiquiatra há anos e que ainda usa medicamentos para dormir e estabilizar o humor. “Estou um pouco melhor, porque eu passo com psiquiatra já há muitos anos. Então, ele passa sempre os mesmos remédios para mim."

Um atestado médico obtido pelo g1 registra que Esther era acompanhada por um quadro de “ansiedade aguda com sintomas somáticos”. O documento descreve disforia, cansaço, fadiga, dificuldade de concentração, labilidade emocional e alterações no sono e no apetite, além de “importante impacto funcional”, com prejuízos nas atividades cotidianas.

No interrogatório, médico nega acusações

No interrogatório à polícia, Osmar negou as acusações feitas por Esther e afirmou que nunca praticou qualquer ato de conotação sexual durante os atendimentos. Ele ainda disse que os exames eram realizados na presença da mãe ou de uma auxiliar.

O médico confirmou que fez um exame retal em Esther, mas afirmou que o procedimento ocorreu uma única vez, com luvas, por suspeita de endometriose.

Osmar também negou ter exibido vídeos pornográficos. Ele contou que, às vezes, mostra às pacientes vídeos do YouTube com orientações sobre o uso de bolas de pompoarismo e sobre autoexame das mamas.

Sobre as fotografias, confirmou ter feito uma sessão com Esther no consultório, mas afirmou que as imagens faziam parte de uma campanha de combate ao câncer de mama. Segundo ele, a jovem autorizou as fotos, levou o próprio figurino e recebeu os arquivos. O médico negou ter mostrado fotos de pacientes nuas e afirmou que não mantém esse tipo de arquivo.

O inquérito não foi finalizado e o médico ainda não foi indiciado.

articles.body:
Mesmo respaldados por uma decisão judicial, jornalistas voltaram a ser barrados nesta quinta-feira (24) ao tentarem entrar na Casa Branca, em Washington, nos Estados Unidos, afirmaram o site de notícias Politico e as redes de TV CNN e MS NOW.

Um repórter do Politico foi impedido de entrar na Casa Branca nesta quinta-feira, relatou o portal.

➡️ Os três haviam sido banidos pelo presidente Donald Trump de entrar na Casa Branca , onde jornalistas comparecem diariamente para cobrir atos e pronunciamentos do governo dos EUA. Na quarta-feira (23), no entanto, a Justiça americana determinou que o governo não pode barrar os jornalistas e que voltasse a permitir o acesso dos veículos.

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, fala com a imprensa ao retornar à Casa Branca após cumprimentar o presidente chinês Xi Jinping na Base Aérea Conjunta Andrews, no gramado sul da Casa Branca, em Washington, DC, EUA, em 23 de setembro de 2026 — Foto: Evan Vucci/Reuters

Segundo um juiz federal, a proibição imposta aos veículos de comunicação provavelmente é inconstitucional. O juiz Tim Kelly emitiu a decisão em uma ação movida pelos veículos de comunicação contra a proibição anunciada pelo presidente americano em 18 de setembro, em um revés significativo para Trump em uma de suas maiores disputas com a imprensa.

Kelly ordenou que o governo Trump devolva imediatamente as credenciais de imprensa dos três veículos e proibiu as autoridades de aplicar a restrição por 14 dias. O juiz rejeitou a alegação do governo de que a proibição teria sido motivada por preocupações com a segurança nacional.

"O processo não apresenta suporte factual para a alegação dos réus de que a revogação das credenciais permanentes dos autores efetivamente protegerá a segurança nacional ou de que ela será colocada em risco caso o tribunal determine o restabelecimento das credenciais enquanto o litígio estiver em andamento", afirmou.

Ele acrescentou que o próprio Trump declarou que a proibição ocorreu devido à "suposta falta de veracidade e negatividade" das reportagens publicadas pelos veículos.

Repórter da CNN faz transmissão ao vivo em rua de Washington, nos Estados Unidos, após ser impedida de entrar na Casa Branca por determinação de Donald Trump, em 19 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Anna Rose Layden/ Reuters

A Casa Branca e representantes dos três veículos não responderam imediatamente aos pedidos de comentário.

Trump havia afirmado nas redes sociais que os três veículos "não deveriam ter permissão para escrever ou divulgar constantemente FICÇÃO e MENTIRAS", enquanto advogados do Departamento de Justiça tentaram justificar a medida com base em razões de segurança nacional.

CNN, MS NOW e Politico processaram Trump e outros integrantes de seu governo na Justiça federal em Washington na segunda-feira, argumentando que a proibição violava as garantias da Primeira Emenda da Constituição dos EUA sobre liberdade de expressão e de imprensa, além de seus direitos ao devido processo legal.

Os veículos solicitaram uma ordem temporária que restabelecesse imediatamente seu acesso à Casa Branca enquanto a disputa judicial estivesse em curso.

A batalha jurídica acontece poucas semanas antes das eleições legislativas de 3 de novembro, nas quais os republicanos de Trump tentam manter o controle do Congresso. As taxas de aprovação do presidente estão nos níveis mais baixos já registrados em pesquisas de opinião, em meio a preocupações com temas como a guerra com o Irã e a inflação.

Em audiência realizada na quarta-feira, Kelly afirmou que dois precedentes da Corte de Apelações dos EUA para o Circuito do Distrito de Columbia deixam claro que jornalistas têm direito ao devido processo legal antes que suas credenciais para a Casa Branca sejam revogadas. O juiz acrescentou que a Casa Branca aparentemente não ofereceu aos veículos afetados uma oportunidade significativa de contestar a perda de acesso.

Um advogado que representa os veículos afirmou a Kelly que eles foram banidos sem aviso prévio ou oportunidade de contestação, exigências previstas em lei. Segundo ele, a medida foi sem precedentes, desarrazoada e representou uma punição severa.

Um advogado do Departamento de Justiça argumentou que o governo Trump apresentou justificativa suficiente para a revogação das credenciais em cartas enviadas aos veículos na terça-feira. O juiz, porém, demonstrou ceticismo em relação a esse argumento, observando que as cartas foram enviadas depois que a revogação já havia ocorrido e após o ajuizamento da ação.

Em documento apresentado à Justiça na terça-feira, o Departamento de Justiça sustentou que o acesso à Casa Branca é um privilégio, e não um direito, e que o presidente tem autoridade para suspender o acesso de organizações de notícias.

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, fala com repórteres antes de embarcar no Air Force One na Base Aérea Conjunta Andrews, em Maryland, em 9 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Foto de BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI/AFP

Uma coalizão de grupos de defesa da liberdade de imprensa e dezenas de empresas jornalísticas protocolou na quarta-feira um parecer em apoio aos três veículos. Eles argumentaram que "retirar de jornalistas e veículos de comunicação seus direitos em razão de uma percepção sobre sua linha editorial viola décadas de jurisprudência da Suprema Corte".

O documento foi assinado, entre outros, pelo Comitê de Repórteres para a Liberdade de Imprensa, Reuters, Washington Post e Fox News.

articles.title: Forever Chemicals: Ground Zero
articles.summary: Pervasive, persistent and poisonous: How one US company helped pollute the world with forever chemicals.
articles.body:
Pervasive, persistent and poisonous: How one US company helped pollute the world with forever chemicals.

When scientists discovered a new class of chemicals in the 1940s, they knew they had struck gold. Polyfluoroalkyl substances, known as PFAS, are nearly indestructible – resistant to heat, cold, oil and water. They’ve been used in everything from cookware to cosmetics and from pizza boxes to pesticides. But they also don’t biodegrade in the environment, and some of them are toxic. US corporate giant 3M was the first to mass-manufacture PFAS and allowed them to pollute the environment around its facilities for decades despite being aware of their harmful effects.

articles.title: CNN e MS NOW dizem que receberam acesso à Casa Branca | G1
articles.standfirst: Veículos haviam sido barrados por Trump, mas juiz federal determinou que governo devolvesse credenciais e permitisse novamente a entrada de jornalistas.
articles.summary: Veículos haviam sido barrados por Trump, mas juiz federal determinou que governo devolvesse credenciais e permitisse novamente a entrada de jornalistas.
articles.body:
Os veículos de comunicação americanos MS NOW e CNN afirmaram nesta quinta-feira (24) que receberam autorização para voltar a ter acesso à Casa Branca , em Washington.

A informação foi divulgada depois de jornalistas dos dois veículos e do site Politico terem sido barrados ao tentar entrar na sede do governo dos Estados Unidos, apesar de uma decisão judicial que determinava a liberação do acesso.

Na quarta-feira (23), um juiz federal determinou que o governo do presidente Donald Trump devolvesse imediatamente as credenciais de imprensa dos três veículos e permitisse novamente o acesso à Casa Branca .

O juiz Tim Kelly determinou que a restrição não poderia ser aplicada durante 14 dias, enquanto o processo movido pelos veículos de comunicação contra o governo tramita na Justiça .

Nesta quinta-feira, porém, um repórter do Politico foi novamente impedido de entrar na Casa Branca, segundo o próprio portal. CNN e MS NOW também relataram que seus jornalistas enfrentaram restrições.

Repórter da CNN faz transmissão ao vivo em rua de Washington, nos Estados Unidos, após ser impedida de entrar na Casa Branca por determinação de Donald Trump, em 19 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Anna Rose Layden/ Reuters

Trump proibiu entrada de jornalistas críticos

Os três veículos haviam sido proibidos pelo governo Trump de entrar na Casa Branca na sexta-feira passada (18). Jornalistas credenciados costumam ter acesso diário ao espaço para acompanhar pronunciamentos e reuniões, além de apurar informações com autoridades e funcionários públicos.

Segundo Trump, os três meios eram responsáveis por disseminar desinformação a seu respeito. Como justificativa ao bloqueio, a Casa Branca alegou que o acesso às dependências eram um privilégio , não um direito.

Na decisão, Kelly afirmou que a proibição provavelmente é inconstitucional. O juiz também rejeitou a justificativa apresentada pelo governo de que a medida teria sido motivada por questões de segurança nacional.

Não há suporte factual suficiente para afirmar que a retirada das credenciais dos veículos protegeria a segurança nacional, disse o juiz, ou que o restabelecimento do acesso representaria uma ameaça.

A decisão judicial é temporária e vale enquanto o processo continua na Justiça americana.

articles.title: Caiado diz que resultados de Goiás podem ser levados ao Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Em caminhada na região noroeste, Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) falou sobre mostrar para os brasileiros o trabalho que realizou enquanto governador de Goiás.
articles.summary: Em caminhada na região noroeste, Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) falou sobre mostrar para os brasileiros o trabalho que realizou enquanto governador de Goiás.
articles.body:
Ronaldo Caiado, candidato do Partido Social Democrático (PSD) à Presidência da República, realizou campanha em Goiás, nesta quinta-feira (24), na região noroeste de Goiânia , ao lado da esposa Gracinha Caiado (UP). Na ocasião, o candidato reuniu políticos e apoiadores na Praça da Feira, no bairro Morada do Sol, visitou comércios e ouviu o empresariado da região.

“A minha presença em Goiás é para poder mostrar para os brasileiros que tudo aquilo que eu falo é porque nós já fizemos no estado”, destacou o candidato.

Em entrevista ao g1 , o ex-governador disse que os resultados conquistados durante sua gestão em Goiás podem ser ampliados para o Brasil. Durante o ato, ele citou projetos desenvolvidos no estado nas áreas da saúde, segurança pública e programas sociais.

“Goiás cresce o dobro do Brasil neste momento. Para vocês terem uma ideia, eu tenho 88% de aprovação. Entre 10 goianos, 9 aqui me apoiam. Por quê? Porque o Caiado fez o trabalho que a sociedade deseja”, afirmou.

Ronaldo e Gracinha Caiado durante agenda em Goiânia — Foto: Eliane Barros/g1 Goiás

Ao falar sobre os programas sociais, Caiado destacou que, durante sua gestão, milhares de goianos saíram da condição de extrema pobreza.

“Aqui nós implantamos os programas sociais de emancipação das pessoas. Em Goiás, foram 602 mil pessoas que saíram da condição de extrema pobreza, e hoje vivem de sua renda própria”, afirmou.

Segundo ele, as iniciativas de capacitação profissional desenvolvidas durante o seu governo, como o programa Colégios Tecnológicos do Estado de Goiás (COTEC), garantiu que os recursos chegassem às pessoas que buscavam trabalhar e conquistar autonomia financeira. “Isto é trabalhar para que o dinheiro chegue de forma correta a quem quer produzir e ter a sua renda e a sua dignidade”, disse.

Na área da saúde, o ex-governador afirmou que sua gestão promoveu a regionalização do atendimento com a implantação de hospitais em diferentes regiões do estado.

“Nós fizemos uma verdadeira regionalização no estado. Implantamos hospitais em Itumbiara, no sul, no entorno de Brasília, no norte do estado de Goiás, no Vale do Araguaia, também chegando à região oeste e sudoeste”, afirmou.

Além disso, o ex-governador também disse que tem um “passado digno” e que não está envolvido em escândalos de corrupção, como o caso do Banco Master.

“Eu sou um homem que tem um passado digno. Eu ganhei a vida com dignidade e sustento a minha família de uma maneira transparente. Você não vê o Caiado envolvido em bandalheira, em corrupção, em rachadinha, nem em Banco Master. Dá um Google no Caiado, venha para Goiás e veja se eu não sou o homem preparado para governar o Brasil”, destacou.

Caiado também afirmou que pretende criar, caso seja eleito, um programa de inteligência artificial voltado ao combate ao crime organizado e à lavagem de dinheiro. Segundo ele, a proposta, chamada de “Sentinela”, reuniria informações de órgãos como o Coaf, Receita Federal, Comissão de Valores Mobiliários (CVM) e Polícia Federal.

“Eu quero desenvolver no Ministério da Segurança Pública a IA Sentinela, uma Inteligência Artificial num programa chamado Sentinela, onde eu terei as informações para repassar para todas as autoridades do Brasil do Coaf, também da CVM, se teve aumento de patrimônio, da Receita Federal e também da inteligência da Polícia Federal”, afirmou.

Caiado disse ainda que o objetivo é permitir que governadores, prefeitos e polícias estaduais tenham acesso a informações sobre pessoas e empresas que, segundo ele, estejam atuando fora da legalidade.

“É a maneira de asfixiar o crime, é a maneira de conter essa lavagem de dinheiro”, declarou.

articles.title: Gamer granny is oldest female Fortnite streamer in world record book
articles.summary: Cath Bowie, from Moray, began playing the online shooter in 2017 and now has an audience of around 24,000 followers.
articles.body:
A 78-year-old Scottish grandmother has been named the world's oldest female Fortnite streamer by Guinness World Records.

Cath Bowie, who is originally from Moray but now lives in Inverurie, began playing the online shooter in 2017 and now has an audience of more than 24,000 followers.

She was introduced to the game by her grandson, who was 17 at the time, and says no-one is "ever too old to start gaming".

Known on Fortnite her username grumpygran1948, Cath features in the Guinness World Records Gamer's Edition 2027.

Fortnite is one of the most popular video games in the world, putting up to 100 players against each other in a fight to be the last one standing.

Cath had tried video games before, but none fully sparked her interest until she discovered Fortnite.

She then bought her own console, but her grandson doubted she would grow a following as a streamer.

She said: "As a young guy, he just couldn't believe that his grandma would do such a thing and suggested that nobody would join me or watch me.

"Saying that was like a red rag to a bull to me. I would show him that I could do it.

"Twenty four thousand followers later and he doesn't mention it. I wonder why?"

Cath said she loves the challenge the game gives her and plays it every day.

She told the BBC's Radio Scotland Breakfast programme: "It's a lovely, lovely game. The one I play is Battle Royale Last Man Standing and you go into it either as a solo, duo or squad.

"You're trying to get the better of your opponents and eliminate them.

"But there's no blood on the scene - you just shoot somebody and they either crawl about until they die or they're just obliterated with the one shot. So there isn't any mess - nothing like that."

Cath said the community of people playing the game was more important than the game itself.

"I play with some wonderful folk - from the UK, quite a few from the USA, from Canada, New Zealand and Australia," she said.

"It's super meeting all these folk. The chat we have, it's lovely - I've had folk with me for quite a few years now."

Alice Bell, editor of Guinness World Records Gamer's Edition 2027, said: "At Guinness World Records we believe gaming is for everyone.

"This edition showcases gamers of different generations and cultures from around the world.

articles.title: Edinburgh Zoo's red panda goes to the vet for toothache
articles.summary: Red panda Bruce laid on his back under a general anaesthetic, as vets removed the problem tooth and checked him for other illnesses.
articles.body:
Edinburgh Zoo's red panda makes a visit to the dentist look easy after having his tooth removed during a health check-up.

Keepers noticed that Bruce was not eating his food. They sent him to Royal Zoological Society of Scotland vets who discovered he was suffering from toothache.

Eleven-year-old Bruce laid on his back under a general anaesthetic, as they removed the problem tooth and checked him for other illnesses.

The endangered red panda, who arrived in Edinburgh in 2016, was given a clean bill of health and returned to his habitat.

Red pandas are native to the eastern Himalayas and south western China.

Bruce is now the only red panda at the zoo and is the grandfather of Priya, a female red panda who moved to the Highland Wildlife Park earlier this year.

Edinburgh Zoo's baby red panda Roxie was three-months-old when she died from stress caused by fireworks on Bonfire Night in 2024 .

Her mother Ginger also died unexpectedly five days earlier at the age of nine.

Red pandas have become an endangered species, mainly due to habitat loss, human interference and poaching.

They are not related to giant pandas but rather closer to raccoons, skunks and weasels.

The World Wildlife Fund (WWF) estimates there are fewer than 10,000 red pandas left in the wild.

They are classified as endangered by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN).

articles.title: In 1994, Michael Tilson Thomas paid $1.4 million for the historic 1906 San Francisco mansion; after a 2012 remodel and 32 years as his home, the 7,090-sq-ft home is now on the market for nearly $10 million
articles.summary: Legendary musician, conductor and composer Michael Tilson Thomas’s Pacific Heights residence has hit the market.
articles.body: Legendary musician, conductor and composer Michael Tilson Thomas’s Pacific Heights residence has hit the market. The historic mansion at 2670 Pierce Street was Thomas’s home for 32 years, where he lived with his husband and longtime manager, Joshua Robison. Thomas died in April 2026, just two months after Robison’s death. Now, for the first time since the 12-time Grammy winner bought the property in 1994, the four-level San Francisco home is up for sale, with an asking price of $9.85 million, according to Robb Report.Historic Pacific Heights addressThis Pacific Heights mansion belonged to musical royalty for three decades. But the mansion has its own history. The mansion was built in 1906 by San Francisco contractor Jeremiah Deneen for himself, according to Anne and Arthur Bloomfield, the authors of ‘Gables and Fables: A Portrait of San Francisco’s Pacific Heights’. Deneen was a pivotal figure in San Francisco’s post-earthquake reconstruction, selected by Mayor James Phelan for the ‘Committee of Fifty’, a body tasked with reshaping the city’s urban landscape. He built and designed the Pierce Street house with his unique architectural ideas.The 7,090-sq-ft home is curated with a blend of Arts and Crafts, Tudor Revival and Elizabethan traditions. The home’s exterior features these styles, with steep-roofed dormer windows and a distinctive mix of timber and brick façade. Inside, the large living and dining rooms, fireplaces, built-in cabinets and exposed beams reflect these classic architectural styles.According to the listing agent, Helena Zaludova of Compass, these characteristics ‘give the house a recognisable identity on the street’. “What makes those architectural details appealing today is the warmth they bring to a house of this scale.”Michael Tilson Thomas bought the property in 1994When Michael Tilson Thomas and Joshua Robison purchased the property in 1994, they immediately recognised its potential, both as a residence and a place befitting a life devoted to music. For nearly three decades, the mansion became their sanctuary. Its capacious rooms and soaring ceilings echoed with their music and also welcomed hundreds of famous guests, including conductors, composers, performers like Linda Ronstadt and architects like Frank Gehry.The couple preserved the mansion’s historic details while adding modern amenities to it. A 2012 remodel brought the home into contemporary luxury without erasing its character. The kitchen was significantly updated. Now it features upscale appliances, custom cabinetry and a glassed-in breakfast nook that floods the space with light. The dramatic staircase, retained from Deneen’s original design, leads to a media room and two dedicated offices. On the top level, beneath angled ceilings and oversized skylights, sits a family room and lounge with breathtaking bay views. The couple also added a guest suite to the mansion, along with a home gym and wine storage, expanding the home’s functionality without sacrificing its historic soul.What the buyer getsThe mansion has seven bedrooms, five full bathrooms and two partial bathrooms across its four levels. Beyond the primary residence, the updated kitchen and formal dining room, both retaining fireplaces, anchor the home’s living spaces. There is built-in cabinetry throughout, and the exposed-beam ceilings maintain visual continuity with the original design.The home sits on a 2,130-sq-ft corner lot with trees in the front and a private garden, which the listing agents describe as a ‘rear garden oasis’.After the musician’s death, the home is now being sold through a trust. “When I first saw the home, I could feel the beauty and love that had lived here. The two Yamaha pianos, Michael’s composing keyboard and the extraordinary personal collection of musical scores and artefacts made his creative life feel so present. Even now, with their personal belongings and furnishings removed, the house still speaks that same language of sophistication and warmth,” an anonymous estate trustee shared in a press statement.For buyers seeking a property where architectural history meets modern convenience, this Pacific Heights address is a seamless fit. Needless to say, it comes with its famous history and lineage.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: GB Energy boss defends Aberdeen job creation record
articles.summary: Dan McGrail says the state-owned renewables investment firm is directly recruiting two people a week, and its funding is benefitting thousands more.
articles.body:
The boss of Great British Energy has defended the state-owned company's job creation record after claims its impact on Aberdeen has been oversold.

Chief executive Dan McGrail said the firm was recruiting about "two people a week" for its Aberdeen-based HQ and the total would eventually rise to around 300.

GB Energy, which featured in Labour's 2024 election manifesto, was established last year to provide investment for UK clean energy projects.

McGrail said it had already made three major investments which would indirectly trigger about 1,500 jobs and it had a target of helping to create 10,000 jobs by 2030.

More stories from North East Scotland, Orkney and Shetland

Listen to news from North East Scotland on BBC Sounds

When Aberdeen was chosen for the headquarters of Great British Energy, the UK government said it reflected the city's long association with the oil and gas sector, as well as its growing role in offshore wind and other renewable technologies.

On Tuesday, King Charles formally opened its offices at Marischal Square on the city's Broad Street, which McGrail said signalled it was "open for business".

There has been controversy, however, over the number of jobs the firm will bring to Aberdeen after chairman Jurgen Maier initially suggested in 2024 that 1,000 might be directly employed over the next 20 years.

Last year, McGrail who by then had been appointed chief executive, clarified that his plan was to recruit about 300 people at the Aberdeen headquarters by 2030

He told BBC Radio Scotland Breakfast: "The only thing that's changed since then is that we're getting on with it.

"We are recruiting about two people a week at the moment.

"What's the most important thing is how effective those people are when they come on board."

McGrail added: "The thing that we really ought to be measured on... is about the impact that our investments make.

"We've been given a budget to invest in the energy transition and to give a stake to the public in the energy transition.

"We've set a target to create 10,000 additional jobs as a result of our activities by 2030."

But Douglas Lumsden, Scottish Conservative MP for Aberdeen South, said progress was falling "far short of the expectations they created".

He said: "If it's only adding two employees a week, it raises serious questions about how the government expects to reach its stated target of 300 staff in any reasonable timeframe."

The idea for Great British Energy was first put forward by Sir Keir Starmer when Labour was in opposition, and it became a major policy pledge in the run up to the 2024 general election.

The party also claimed that as part of a wider clean energy strategy, it could help cut average household energy bills by £300 a year.

Labour has promised to back Great British Energy with £8.3bn of funding over the lifetime of the current parliament.

The firm's first investment was in the Pentland Offshore Wind Farm, being constructed by a Danish company off the coast of Caithness.

It has also invested in a hydrogen manufacturing project in Sheffield and solar panels at schools and NHS sites, mainly in England.

McGrail said in Scotland it had been working through the Scottish government's Community and Renewable Energy Scheme (Cares), and its funding had benefitted 70 local Scottish projects.

articles.title: Israel’s Netanyahu takes the U.N. stage facing global isolation and a fight for his political future
articles.summary: As Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pleads his country’s case at the United Nations General Assembly, his target audience will likely be Israeli voters.
articles.body: TEL AVIV — Even as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pleads his country’s case to the world at the United Nations General Assembly on Thursday, his target audience will likely be closer to home: Israeli voters ahead of next month’s crucial elections. Netanyahu arrived in New York on Thursday for what appears to be a whirlwind trip that will highlight the growing isolation of the U.S. ally over its assault on the Gaza Strip. With only a handful of diplomatic meetings on the sidelines of the assembly and President Donald Trump’s focus firmly on his summit with China’s Xi Jinping, the prime minister looks set to return to Israel shortly after his address to be back in time for the major Jewish holiday of Sukkot on Friday evening. “I am leaving tonight for New York in order to defend, from the U.N. podium, Israel and IDF soldiers,” the prime minister said in a video Wednesday night before he left. “You hear the terrible lies that are being spread there.” Netanyahu is likely to address an almost empty chamber as delegates observe an annual tradition of walking out in protest over the conduct of Israel’s war in the Gaza Strip. But that spectacle will likely play well among the premier’s domestic supporters, for whom he has styled himself as a defiant truth teller standing up for Israel on the global stage. While much of the world has condemned Israel for the huge loss of civilian life and continuing humanitarian tragedy in Gaza, Netanyahu’s primary domestic challenge comes from an Israeli right wing that accuses him of not being tough enough in the country’s multifront war on Iran and its proxy groups. “The main reason that brings him to the UN General Assembly this time is the opportunity to talk, using the UN microphone, to his voters in Israel, in his polished English, in a speech that of course will be accompanied by exaggerated descriptions of his great achievements,” Ephraim Ganor, a political and strategic affairs expert, wrote in the right-leaning Israeli newspaper Ma’ariv. The few hints that Netanyahu has given about the subject of his speech have focused on populist, patriotic causes. In a video posted to social media on Tuesday, Netanyahu took aim at a popular target: New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who had pledged to arrest him for crimes against humanity before later acknowledging that he lacked the jurisdiction to do so. Appearing to adopt the posture of a professional wrestler and looking straight into the camera, Netanyahu accused the mayor of supporting Hamas — which Mamdani has strenuously denied — and fomenting riots against New York Jews. He added that he would “tell the truth about you” and “tell the truth about our heroic soldiers.” Asked about Netanyahu’s comments, Mamdani told a news conference Tuesday that the Israeli military had killed an 11-year-old boy in a zone deemed safe in Gaza, “so that is what I have to say to his video.” Netanyahu’s mention of Israel soldiers appears to be a reference to “NAZA,” a documentary made by two Israeli filmmakers in which 24 anonymous Israelis, described as military and intelligence officials, talk about the cynical process by which the country’s military evaluated the need for civilian deaths during the Gaza war. A popular target that has riled Israeli leaders ahead of the elections, “NAZA” has earned plaudits abroad but condemnation at home. Politicians have stumbled over themselves to publicly condemn the documentary in the harshest terms, with some demanding a criminal investigation into the duo and even that they be stripped of Israeli citizenship. In another hint on Wednesday night, Netanyahu, who has a history of peppering his General Assembly speeches with props, gags and gimmicks, said his speech would include “surprises.” Last year, he told the audience that his speech was being broadcast into Gaza through massive loudspeakers and streamed to mobile phones so that Israeli hostages trapped in Gaza could hear him speak. He also wore an oversized QR code on his jacket, encouraging audiences to activate the code to visit a website with a video showing Hamas’ attacks on Israel in October 2023 in which about 1,200 people were killed and which sparked the latest round of fighting. Israel’s subsequent war in Gaza has killed more than 75,000 people, according to Palestinian health officials. In the years before that, Netanyahu brandished regional maps to make his points. Two years ago, he displayed two maps that showed the “blessing” of Israel’s influence contrasted with the “curse” of Iran’s expanding power. And in 2012, more than a decade before the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in what they said was an attempt to keep the Islamic Republic from getting a nuclear weapon, Netanyahu held up a cartoon image of an Iranian nuclear weapon with a “red line” for its maximum enrichment level.

articles.title: Gary Anderson: On-the-run killer appears in Donegal court
articles.summary: Gary Anderson had been serving life in prison for the murder of Karol Kelly in Londonderry in 2018.
articles.body:
An on-the-run killer who absconded after being permitted to attend his father's funeral in Northern Ireland 10 days ago has appeared in court in the Republic of Ireland, where he was arrested on Wednesday.

Gary Anderson, 29, appeared at a special sitting of Letterkenny District Court on Thursday following his arrest at a campsite near Buncrana, by An Garda Síochána (Irish police).

He had been serving life in prison for the murder of Karol Kelly in Londonderry in 2018.

The court was told Anderson is charged with being present at Fahan Marina caravan and campsite on 23 September, having escaped from Maghaberry Prison, contrary to Section 3(1) of the Criminal Law (Jurisdiction) Act 1976.

Garda Det Jason Conroy gave details of the arrest, charge and caution during the hearing on Thursday.

The detective said Anderson was arrested at about 13:44 local time on Wednesday at Fahan Marina campsite and was told why he was being arrested but made no reply.

At 20:47, he was charged, handed a copy of the charge sheet and again made no reply, the court was told.

Garda Sgt Jim Collins told the court that there had been no application for bail from Anderson's legal representatives at that time.

Collins said he was seeking directions from the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) in the case and was seeking to have the accused remanded in custody.

He applied to Judge Emile Daly for an adjournment in the case to allow for these directions.

Judge Daly adjourned the case for Anderson to appear by videolink at Letterkenny District Court later this month.

His solicitor said that while he understood Judge Daly could not direct that Anderson be held in a prison other than Castlerea Prison in County Roscommon, he asked the judge to recommend another prison because of what he termed "other parties involved".

On Thursday Karol Kelly's sister Francesca confirmed that she met the Justice Minister Naomi Long to discuss the matter.

articles.title: Seattle’s 'Inconvenience Store': A former 7-Eleven reopened as an art shop selling pre-tangled USB cables, a 'landline iPhone', fake corn dogs and useless everyday items
articles.summary: A former 7-Eleven in downtown Seattle has been given an unusual second life as an interactive art shop where familiar convenience-store products have been
articles.body: A former 7-Eleven in downtown Seattle has been given an unusual second life as an interactive art shop where familiar convenience-store products have been transformed into deliberately impractical artworks. Called the 'Inconvenience Store', the exhibition keeps much of the former shop's layout, including its aisles, checkout area, refrigerator and hot-food counter, but fills them with creations from more than 70 artists. Visitors can find pre-tangled USB cables, a 'landline iPhone' that plays U2's 'Vertigo' when answered, beeswax egg candles, bags made from Cheetos and Lay's packaging, fake corn dogs and other strange reinterpretations of everyday objects. The exhibition officially opened on September 19 as part of Seattle's WALKDONTRUN arts marathon and is scheduled to remain at the site through mid-2027.Seattle's 'Inconvenience Store' turns a former 7-Eleven into artThe exhibition occupies the former 7-Eleven at 1524 Third Avenue, at the corner of Third Avenue and Pine Street in downtown Seattle. Instead of stripping away the shop's original identity, organisers have used the existing convenience-store setting as part of the artwork. The checkout counter, aisles, refrigerator and hot-food area remain, but the products have been replaced with handmade art.The project was created by Seattle artists and curators Lilia Deering and Mary Anne Carter, who previously worked together on 'STÖR', an IKEA-inspired art project. Their latest exhibition similarly uses a familiar retail environment to make art more approachable to people who may not normally visit traditional galleries.More than 70 artists, mostly from the Seattle area, contributed pieces to the exhibition. Their work is arranged across 14 departments, imitating the organisation of a conventional convenience store.Pre-tangled USB cables and other deliberately inconvenient itemsThe shop's central idea is to take ordinary convenience-store products and remove the convenience.One example is a pre-tangled USB cable, turning one of the most familiar minor frustrations of modern life into an art object. Other pieces include beeswax candles shaped like eggs, keychains resembling snacks such as Nerds, Oreos and Goldfish, and shoulder bags made from discarded Cheetos and Lay's packaging.Another artwork turns a candle into a yardstick. It resembles a measuring tool, but naturally becomes shorter every time it is lit. The exhibition also includes a range of other handmade reinterpretations of familiar products, organised as though shoppers were moving through an ordinary convenience store.The former hot-food counter has also been transformed. Instead of serving food, it displays artist-made versions of items including fake corn dogs with googly eyes and other playful designs.A 'landline iPhone' that plays only one songAmong the stranger objects is a 'landline iPhone', which deliberately strips away much of what makes a smartphone useful. When the phone is answered, it plays U2's 'Vertigo'.The exhibition also contains an ATM-inspired sound sculpture and a former refrigerator that has been turned into a small gallery displaying rotating artwork. In this setting, even the shop's fixtures have become part of the experience rather than simply serving their original purpose.More than 70 artists contributed to the shopThe creators have divided the exhibition into 14 departments, including sections resembling food and pantry, health and beauty, and office supplies. The approach allows visitors to navigate the exhibition much as they would a normal shop, except that almost everything on the shelves is an artwork.The organisers have described the project as a way of challenging the emphasis on efficiency and mass production. Handmade art can take more time and effort than mass-produced goods, making the deliberately inconvenient theme part of the exhibition's wider idea.The familiar shop environment is also intended to make buying art less intimidating. Instead of encountering artworks in a traditional gallery with less obvious pricing, visitors can browse shelves and see prices attached to individual pieces.Artworks range from $1 to $10,000Despite its appearance, the Inconvenience Store is not simply a novelty display. The artworks are available for purchase, with reported prices ranging from $1 to $10,000.The exhibition therefore combines the experience of shopping with that of visiting an art gallery. Visitors can browse the shelves, examine the unusual objects and, if they want, take one of the artworks home.The exhibition is free to visitThe Inconvenience Store officially opened on September 19, 2026, during Seattle's WALKDONTRUN arts marathon. The event's official schedule lists the exhibition at 1524 Third Avenue, with opening-day hours from noon to 4pm.The exhibition is free to visit and is scheduled to operate on Saturdays and Sundays from noon to 4pm. Current event listings say it is expected to remain at the location until June 27, 2027.For visitors expecting the convenience of a normal 7-Eleven, the new shop offers almost the opposite experience, a place where a USB cable is deliberately tangled, a phone has only one job and even a corn dog is something you cannot eat.You use AI every day. articles.title: Cauvery row: Karnataka CM says ‘will release water only if available’; Tamil Nadu flags 20 TMC deficit
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Wednesday said the state would release Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu only if it was available, noting
articles.body: BENGALURU: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Wednesday said the state would release Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu only if it was available, noting that inflows into its reservoirs had stopped due to a lack of rainfall.Shivakumar said the state government was under significant pressure and planned to file an appeal regarding the matter, news agency ANI reported.“We will release water only if it is available; however, the inflow into our reservoirs has stopped. We are under immense pressure as the rains have ceased, and we intend to file an appeal. I will review the matter of filing an appeal during the special session meeting this evening. The Irrigation Minister is with us,” said Shivakumar.Earlier on Wednesday, the Supreme Court considered Tamil Nadu’s plea seeking release of its share of Cauvery water amid competing claims by the two states over water availability.Tamil Nadu alleged a shortfall of 20 TMC, while Karnataka cited drought conditions in its basin, ANI reported.Tamil Nadu told a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta that it had suffered crop losses due to inadequate water.Appearing for Tamil Nadu, senior counsel CS Vaidyanathan said the state had already lost its Purvai crop, an early or late Kharif crop, due to the shortage of water.He alleged that Karnataka was “taking all the water” and said Tamil Nadu was seeking enforcement of the Cauvery water-sharing arrangement.The bench asked Tamil Nadu about the extent of the alleged shortfall. Vaidyanathan said Tamil Nadu had assessed the deficit at 20 TMC, while Karnataka had put it at 16 TMC.He alleged that the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee and the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) had failed to adequately address the shortfall and sought directions to make up the deficit, ANI reported.Karnataka opposed the plea, with senior counsel Shyam Divan telling the bench that the state was facing a drought-like situation.He said Karnataka had nevertheless continued releasing water in compliance with directions issued by the CWMA.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: US launches online portal to report visa fraud, misuse; tips can be submitted anonymously
articles.summary: The US State Department has launched a dedicated online portal allowing the public to report suspected visa fraud and misuse involving people, companies,
articles.body: The US State Department has launched a dedicated online portal allowing the public to report suspected visa fraud and misuse involving people, companies, schools and other entities.Announcing the initiative on X, State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said, “A US visa is a privilege, not a right,” urging people to share information that could help authorities identify and act against suspected visa violations.The new reporting system covers several categories, including tourist and business visas, employment visas, student visas and immigrant or family-based visas. It also allows reports involving other forms of suspected immigration or visa fraud.The department has asked those filing complaints to provide as much information as possible about the person or organisation involved. Details may include a person's name, passport or visa number, A-Number, petition or receipt number, date of birth, address, contact details, nationality and social media profiles.Reports can also be filed against companies, educational institutions, law firms and other organisations. Users can provide details such as the organisation's name, address, website, contact information and the names of people associated with it.The portal allows complaints to be submitted anonymously. However, people who provide their name and email address may be contacted by investigators if further information is required.The State Department said reports should include details of the activity believed to involve visa fraud or misuse, along with any additional information or updates about a matter that may have been reported previously.The department warned that knowingly submitting false information could result in fines, imprisonment, or both.According to the department's privacy notice, information submitted through the portal may be used to initiate or support law-enforcement investigations and reviews of immigration-related actions. The information may also be shared with other US or foreign law-enforcement agencies where appropriate.The State Department said its fraud detection and prevention efforts are aimed at stopping attempts to enter the US through fraudulent means or for illegal purposes. It cited examples including falsified documents or travel plans, sham marriages, shell companies, fabricated job offers and birth tourism.The department said suspected criminal activity unrelated to the US immigration system should instead be reported to the appropriate law-enforcement or government authorities. Immediate threats to national security or public safety should also be reported through the relevant emergency channels.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Reported assaults on Britain's rail services rise by more than a third
articles.summary: Recorded incidents of violence and harassment against passengers and rail workers showed a sharp increase in the year to March.
articles.body:
Reports of violent incidents and harassment on rail services "rose substantially" last year, figures from the rail regulator show.

Reported assaults, including physical and verbal, were up 36% in the year to March 2026 compared with the previous year, according to the Office of Rail and Road (ORR).

In total 13,464 assaults against passengers and members of the public were recorded on Britain's mainline railway, the highest number recorded since the series began in 2004.

The ORR said the figures were "concerning" and that it was working with the industry to address the problem.

According to the figures, harassment increased by 52% compared with the previous year and common assaults rose by 30%.

The increase comes against a backdrop of five years of rising reports of incidents and industry campaigns to raise awareness.

Assaults on the mainline railway are recorded according to their type. As a result each incident can lead to reports in more than one category, for example if someone is harassed and then physically assaulted.

There were also 11,289 reported assaults against members of the workforce on the mainline railway, up 12% compared with the previous year.

Of those 2,487 were physical assaults, while more than half (6,390 incidents) involved verbal abuse. The rest were threats.

"We're working with industry and our trade union colleagues to address work-related violence and harassment," said Richard Hines, the ORR's chief inspector of railways.

"This includes understanding where the risks are, putting effective controls in place, encouraging staff to report incidents and providing appropriate support afterwards," he said.

The statistics include mainline rail services in England, Scotland and Wales, but not Northern Ireland. The data release also covers the London Underground, trams, metros and other light rail services.

On the London Underground, recorded assaults increased 20% to 5,534 in the latest year, but reported workforce assaults fell 3% to 3,525.

Transport for London does not record multiple aspects of each incident. Instead it records the most severe aspect reported.

A spokesperson responding on behalf of Network Rail and the train companies said all operators were working to reduce risk and prevent harm by sharing information, improving reporting processes and deploying body-worn cameras.

"Keeping passengers and colleagues safe is at the heart of everything we do," the spokesperson said.

"Violence, abuse and intimidation directed at passengers or staff are completely unacceptable. The rail industry works closely with British Transport Police to investigate incidents, support victims and bring offenders to justice."

The passenger body, Transport Focus, said the ORR's figures supported research it conducted which found personal security was "one of the highest priorities" for passengers. However, only 3% of passengers it surveyed said they were dissatisfied with personal safety at the station.

Transport Focus acknowledged that some of the increase might reflect better reporting. Nevertheless, every incident represented someone negatively affected, it said, adding it would like to see "a much more strategic approach" to tackling the issue.

The RMT union, representing rail industry workers, said the figures corresponded with the union's own figures indicating two-thirds of its members had experienced violence at work.

RMT general secretary Eddie Dempsey called for an increase in staffing on public transport, including an end to lone working, to combat the problem.

"We also clearly need stronger legal protections for public transport workers against assaults at work," he said.

He said cuts to British Transport Police funding had been "disastrous" and called for outsourced security and enforcement staff to be brought in-house "as a matter of urgency".

Other notable figures from the statistical release include that 11 members of the public died at mainline level crossings in the latest year, six more than the previous year. Eight were pedestrians and the others were road vehicle users.

articles.title: Fighting widens across Ethiopia as Tigray clashes escalate
articles.summary: Armed groups clashed with government forces across northern Ethiopia as fears mount of regional spillover.
articles.body:
“They’ve begun an offensive around southern Tigray,” Abdisalam Balema, a member of the Tigray People’s Liberation Front’s (TPLF) central committee, told Al Jazeera by phone from Mekelle, the Tigrayan capital, on Wednesday morning.

“They’re carrying out strikes in many places. We are not sure of the extent of it or whether they will continue, but we will assess it.”

Balema did not know it then, but he was describing the start of a major military escalation.

Fighting intensified across parts of Tigray and later spread to the neighbouring Afar and Amhara regions, pitting federal forces against several armed groups. A day later, Balema told Al Jazeera that the situation had become a “full war”.

Lower-level clashes between federal and Tigrayan forces had been ongoing for weeks, with the federal government carrying out frequent drone strikes, but both sides had repeatedly pulled back from the brink.

The Tigray Army said the federal government had launched a “full-scale offensive” involving infantry, mechanised units and drones, and said its forces had begun counteroffensive operations.

Getachew Reda, a former senior TPLF figure who now advises Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, gave the opposite account of how the fighting began, accusing the TPLF of launching the attack.

The escalation disrupted air travel, as Tigrayan forces seized airports in the region and Ethiopian Airlines suspended flights across Tigray. Local reports also said they had captured Abala, a district capital in neighbouring Afar.

The intensification came days after seven armed movements from across Ethiopia, including the TPLF, announced the formation of the Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival, which committed itself to removing Abiy’s government.

The coalition has brought together the Amhara Fano National Movement and the Oromo Liberation Army, alongside other movements from Somali, Afar and Benishangul-Gumuz areas.

The alliance marked a striking realignment that had been almost a year in the making , bringing together movements with very different histories and grievances against the central government, including forces with bitter histories of conflict among themselves.

In a statement issued as the fighting widened on Wednesday, the alliance said the federal government was attacking its member forces on several fronts and presented their response as part of the broader struggle that had brought the coalition together.

The regional East African bloc IGAD called for hostilities to cease and direct dialogue to resume, while the United Nations has expressed concern over the formation of the new armed coalition and reports of drone attacks.

About three-quarters of a million people were already internally displaced in Tigray because of the earlier war, according to UN migration data.

The alliance grew out of the political realignment that followed the Pretoria agreement, which ended the two-year Tigray war in November 2022. The deal brought peace between Addis Ababa and the TPLF, but fractured the coalition Abiy had assembled to fight the war.

Neither Eritrea nor Amhara forces, whose troops had fought alongside the federal army, were parties to the final agreement, and both later fell out with the federal government.

In Amhara, tensions over plans to dismantle regional forces helped trigger open conflict between the Ethiopian government and Fano fighters, organised under the Amhara Fano National Movement, in 2023. Relations with Eritrea also deteriorated, first over the Pretoria settlement and later over Abiy’s push for access to the Red Sea through Eritrean ports.

The Pretoria agreement also deepened divisions within the TPLF, between figures such as Reda, who continued to defend the settlement, and a faction led by Debretsion Gebremichael that increasingly rejected the political order it had created.

Pretoria “changed the equation”, Faisal Roble, a regional analyst and member of the East African Parliament, told Al Jazeera. “Abiy alienated all of them at different levels.”

The faction led by Debretsion later seized power in Tigray and repaired relations with former enemies, including Fano fighters in Amhara and Eritrea, upending the alliances that had defined the previous war.

The government’s spokeswoman, Billene Seyoum, told the Reuters news agency after the new coalition was announced that its members had already been collaborating with financial backing from Asmara and that the formal declaration confirmed statements by government officials.

Eritrea has repeatedly denied supporting Ethiopian armed groups.

Reda had dismissed the alliance’s chances of ousting the government shortly after it was announced. “I don’t lose sleep over that,” he told state media this week.

“Now it [the TPLF] goes back to the drawing board, and declares Pretoria dead and starts an alliance with the very people who fell out with the federal government because Pretoria was signed,” he added.

Balema, the senior TPLF official, said the party’s decision to join those former enemies reflected its determination not to find itself isolated if the conflict widened again.

“We’ve been forced to ally with other movements who also face an existential threat from the government,” he told Al Jazeera. “We don’t want a repeat of 2020 when we were encircled and alone.”

Balema acknowledged unresolved disputes within the alliance, including competing claims over western Tigray involving Amhara forces, but said the groups had agreed to address them through dialogue.

“We have a political charter, and our aim is to remove the personalist regime of Abiy Ahmed, establish a transitional government, hold a constitutional dialogue and move to elections,” he added, saying “the alliance is in consensus on this.”

“For now it seems like it will work, but when the deeper issues need to be resolved it will test their different constituencies, who have different expectations,” Mohamed Kheir Omer, a researcher focused on the Horn of Africa, told Al Jazeera.

“But right now it isn’t the urgent issue.”

The alliance also draws in the Oromo Liberation Army and a faction of the Ogaden National Liberation Front, movements rooted in older demands for autonomy and self-determination among Ethiopia’s Oromo and Somali populations.

Both had fought the TPLF-dominated government that preceded Abiy and are now allied with the TPLF. Taking office in 2018, promising a break with the old order, Abiy sought to bring both into civilian politics.

The Oromo Liberation Front returned from exile, but disagreements over disarmament left part of its armed wing outside the settlement.

Those fighters continued their armed conflict as the Oromo Liberation Army, and subsequent peace talks with the government failed.

Though the OLA ultimately signed the new alliance agreement, its leader, Jaal Marroo, had described it in the preceding days as a “procedural consensus” rather than a substantive settlement on Ethiopia’s political future.

The ONLF stayed out of armed conflict after its own 2018 peace deal , but later fractured. An overseas faction accuses the government of failing to implement the agreement and eroding Somali autonomy, while the leadership inside Ethiopia’s Somali region denies joining the new alliance.

Abdulkadir Hassan Hirmoge, a spokesperson for the faction that joined, told Al Jazeera that it now regards the 2018 agreement as void.

He said joining the alliance did not mean restarting an armed struggle, but backing its programme of removing Abiy and establishing a transitional government.

Ethiopia’s domestic conflicts are becoming harder to separate from wider rivalries in the Horn, particularly Sudan’s civil war and Addis Ababa’s deteriorating relationship with Eritrea.

Sudan’s army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan has visited Asmara twice since July for talks with Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki, while Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti, the commander of Sudan’s rival Rapid Support Forces, reportedly visited Addis Ababa in late August.

Reuters reported in February that thousands of RSF fighters were being trained at a camp in western Ethiopia, while Sudan has accused Ethiopia, and its ally the United Arab Emirates, which also reportedly backs the RSF, of allowing drones to be launched from its territory into Sudan.

The emerging Ethiopian opposition alignment has touched the same regional network.

Several figures associated with groups now in the alliance attended a meeting in Port Sudan in May, publicly presented as a “people-to-people” initiative.

In July, Abiy told lawmakers: “Let alone Eritrea, the TPLF and Sudan, even if others were added, we do not have an iota of fear regarding Ethiopia’s sovereignty.”

Balema, the senior TPLF official, denied that the alliance was receiving military or logistical support from either Eritrea or Sudan, saying its relationships abroad amounted to political contacts rather than foreign backing.

“We didn’t create the current problem with Eritrea; Abiy did with his demands on its ports, and the same with Somalia,” he said.

“In Sudan, he is now supporting the Rapid Support Forces. He has created his own enemies across the region and we are just picking up the pieces.”

Sudan has recently sought to ease tensions with Addis Ababa. Malik Agar, the second in command of its military-aligned government, said last week that “we do not want to get involved in a war with Ethiopia.”

Jawar Mohammed, an Oromo opposition politician, warned that Ethiopia could nevertheless become an “incongruent battlefield” in which wider regional contests increasingly play out.

“These things are impossible to control,” he said.
